findings.rationale: Sex=1 subgroup at ME: observed outcome rate 0.0128 vs mean predicted 0.1609 (O/E 0.079, noise-adjusted z_noise -6.4), i.e. positives in this subgroup are systematically recorded as negative. The same client shows a persistent positive calibration-in-the-large (CITL +0.074, z=+4.6) with prevalence well below what its features imply, and an anomalous update norm (median norm ratio 4.44, z=+9.2) with near-zero mean cosine, consistent with training on corrupted labels. The CITL is already large in round 1 and feature drift is absent, so the fault is present from the start.

Sex=1 subgroup at CT: observed outcome rate 0.0086 vs mean predicted 0.1274 (O/E 0.068, z_noise -6.4), an under-recording pattern confined to one subgroup. CT also has a positive CITL (+0.065, z=+4.0 with ECE z=+3.2), prevalence 0.054 against predicted 0.12, and an anomalous update size (median norm ratio 3.19, z=+7.8) with reduced cosine to the median update. Calibration bias is already present in round 1 and there is no feature drift, so onset is round 1.

Sex=1 subgroup at HI: observed outcome rate 0.0188 vs mean predicted 0.1333 (O/E 0.141, z_noise -5.9), the same subgroup-specific under-recording seen at CT and ME. HI has a positive CITL (+0.051, z=+3.2) with prevalence about 0.066 against predicted 0.118, and an anomalous update norm (median norm ratio 2.91, z=+7.1) with mean cosine z=-3.3. The CITL is already elevated in round 1 with no feature drift, so onset is round 1.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with update statistics, local performance, per-round drift, feature tails, and subgroup outcomes for Sex, AgeGroup and Income, then confirmed suspicions on the flagged clients. Three clients (ME, CT, HI) show the same signature: under-recorded positives in the Sex=1 subgroup (O/E 0.07 to 0.14, z_noise about -6), persistent positive calibration-in-the-large from round 1, low prevalence relative to predicted risk, and anomalous update norms. I report them as subgroup_bias with onset round 1, with CT and HI at lower confidence than ME. Other flags were not sustained: DE's drift is erratic across rounds without a consistent shift; GU, VI, NH, TN, WY, NC, DE and PR show single-statistic outliers from small clients, consistent with noise; AL's update norm is only weakly elevated (z=+3.5). The AUC of ME is somewhat low (0.77) but not enough to suggest label noise. The budget is fully spent (20.0).
